name: rsi_extreme_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY's 2-bar RSI drops below 5 on 5-second bars, two consecutive 5-second bars have closed aggressively lower — a micro-exhaustion signal driven by retail stop-loss cascades and short-duration momentum algos overshooting into thin intraday order book depth. NIFTY delta-neutral market makers immediately begin buying to rebalance short-gamma hedges, and VWAP-anchored institutional algorithms see sub-benchmark fills worth accumulating when the index is near VWAP. The combined buying pressure creates a snap-back that typically completes within 30-90 seconds. The RSI(36) filter (3-minute trend context) ensures the entry is not against a sustained institutional directional flow where the exhaustion signal would be overridden by continuous repricing.

indicators.name: rsi_2
indicators.purpose: 2-bar RSI at 5s resolution captures micro-exhaustion: both of the last two 5-second bars closed hard in the same direction. Period stays at 2 (not scaled to 24) because the strategy trades the FASTEST exhaustion signal — the moment directional pressure stops, not 10 minutes later. Original used RSI(2) on 1-min for the same reason: minimum look-back to detect immediate current exhaustion. At <5 or >95, the signal is strong enough that even 5-second noise is filtered out.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 36-bar (3-minute) RSI as intraday trend filter. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min bars (14 minutes of context) to avoid fighting strong trends. For a 15-90 second hold, we need trend context but compressed: 3 minutes is enough to identify whether NIFTY is in a strong unidirectional flow (RSI outside 35-65) vs choppy mean-reverting regime. Using 14 minutes (168 bars) would over-anchor to older data when we're trading the next 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: Cumulative VWAP from 09:15 IST, reset each session: sum(close * volume) / sum(volume)
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP anchors institutional benchmark price. RSI(2) extremes occurring within 1% of VWAP (near institutional fair value) have higher reversion probability: VWAP-buying algorithms and market makers are incentivized to defend this level. Extremes more than 1% below VWAP (for longs) may signal a structural downmove, not a micro-exhaustion. No scaling needed — VWAP is cumulative, not a rolling window.

conditions: RSI(close, 2) < 5 (two consecutive 5s bars closed aggressively lower — micro-selling climax)
RSI(close, 36) between 35-65 (3-minute trend is neutral/choppy, not in strong downtrend)
close > VWAP * 0.99 (within 1% below VWAP — micro-flush near fair value, not structural breakdown)
India VIX < 25 (RSI extremes are unreliable signals in panic; index dislocations persist)
buy_ce.confirmation: Signal fires on the bar where RSI(2) drops below threshold — enter at bar close

conditions: RSI(close, 2) > 95 (two consecutive 5s bars closed aggressively higher — micro-buying climax)
RSI(close, 36) between 35-65 (3-minute trend is neutral/choppy, not in strong uptrend)
close < VWAP * 1.01 (within 1% above VWAP — micro-spike near fair value, not structural breakout)
buy_pe.confirmation: Signal fires on the bar where RSI(2) crosses above threshold — enter at bar close

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = ~6 NIFTY spot points. If the index continues directionally after an RSI(2) extreme — meaning selling/buying pressure is sustained past 6 spot points from entry — the micro-exhaustion thesis is wrong and a macro impulse is in play. NIFTY 30-second moves average 2-5 option pts; a 3-pt stop sits just outside normal noise while cutting losing trades before they double.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 NIFTY spot points. Micro-exhaustion snap-backs on NIFTY typically deliver 8-15 spot points within 60-90 seconds as accumulated buying by market makers and VWAP algos unwinds the overshoot. 5 pts captures the lower half of this expected range for a 1:1.67 R:R, requiring directional accuracy ~55% for profitability.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; in high-VIX regimes RSI(2) extremes occur continuously as NIFTY gaps between 5s bars, making limit execution unreliable and the reversion thesis invalid
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; first 15 minutes (09:15-09:30) excluded due to opening auction noise and structurally extreme RSI readings from overnight gap opens that don't represent intraday exhaustion
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is aggregate across all constituents and less meaningful at 5s than individual stock volume
filters.trend_filter: RSI(36) between 35-65 excludes strong trend bars where exhaustion would fight sustained institutional directional flow
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at 5s candle close, no bid-ask spread cost in this pipeline

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — RSI(2) extremes at 5s are frequent; signal quality depends heavily on the RSI(36) and VWAP filters. Edge may compress if more algos implement micro-reversion logic on the index.

adaptation_notes: Original used RSI(2) on 1-min bars across NIFTY 200 stocks with RSI(14) trend filter, VWAP proximity, and VIX<25 gate. Converted to NIFTY index only at 5s with these specific changes: (1) RSI(14) trend filter compressed from 14-min context to 3-min context (RSI(36)) — because we hold 15-90s not 3-15 min, older trend context is irrelevant; (2) VWAP proximity filter preserved at same 1% band — institutional fair value anchoring is equally valid on the index; (3) Stock-specific filters (ADV, same-stock overtrading, earnings events) dropped — not applicable to index; (4) Confirmation signal (RSI crossing above 10 after being below 5) dropped — at 5s resolution the reversion may complete within 1-2 bars, so we enter on the extreme bar itself rather than waiting for confirmation and missing the snap; (5) Stock volume filter dropped — index aggregate volume not meaningful at 5s; (6) RSI(2) period unchanged — the 2-period minimum lookback is correct for detecting immediate exhaustion regardless of bar frequency.
weaknesses: RSI(2) at 5-second resolution produces very frequent signals — RSI(36) and VWAP proximity filters are critical to avoid overtrading noise
NIFTY index is smoother than individual stocks; RSI(2) extremes below 5 / above 95 may be rarer than in the original equity universe, reducing trade frequency
The 3-minute RSI(36) trend filter can lag on sharp news-driven trend days, allowing entries against a nascent sustained move before RSI(36) reflects the new regime
Near-VWAP filter may underperform in opening-drive sessions where price diverges from VWAP for extended periods — the 1% band is relatively tight
